correctness.rationale: For fixed k>=1 and q=2^k, n>=1, the complete accessibility relation makes Diamond tau_a true exactly if at least one of the n labelled worlds carries Boolean type a. Thus failure of the displayed positive edge-disjunction is equivalent to the image support being independent in G. For each independent j-set there are j! S(n,j) onto functions from n worlds, so summing disjoint supports proves M_G(n)=q^n-sum_{j>=1} i_j j! S(n,j), including edgeless, complete and n=1 boundaries (empty image never arises). N_G(n)=q^n-M_G(n) has lower triangular transform with nonzero diagonal n!, hence the first q counts recover every i_j (with i0=1), and equality for all n is exactly equality of independence polynomials within the fixed q type universe. For #P membership, guess nk Boolean bits and test edge co-occurrence in polynomial time for unary n and explicit formula. For hardness, add 2^ceil(log2 r)-r isolates (q<=2r for r>=2), issue q unary-sized queries, invert with polynomial-bit arithmetic to get I_G(1)/2^(q-r)=#IndSet(H); this is a polynomial-time Turing reduction, not parsimonious. Independently enumerated 82 graphs and 424,572 labelled world assignments, 84 padded reductions, and all graph isomorphism classes through order 3; P4 vs triangle+isolate gives identical 1+4z+3z^2 and different two-world truth at types {0,2}. The fixed-G asymptotic follows from j!S(n,j)=j^n+O((j-1)^n), including alpha=1 separately. Verified exact assigned tree from 7 Git blob identities. The independent finite experiments corroborate, but do not prove, the all-n identity, Turing hardness or asymptotic.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact quantitative problem for epistemic co-occurrence formulas on one complete S5 class; an entire infinite model-count spectrum becomes a recoverable graph polynomial and is shown insufficient for logical equivalence. The inverse is a structural identification result rather than merely evaluating one formula, and #P-completeness persists under the severe depth-one positive pair-diamond restriction. The smallest logical collision and exact exponential failure rate delimit the phenomenon naturally. The support lemma, Stirling transform, generic independent-set counting hardness, and graph collision are standard/known ingredients, so value rests on their exact restricted-modal synthesis and inverse complexity classification, not an inflated claim of inventing those constituents. A plausible researcher could use the spectra classification for modal quantitative identifiability and expressive-fragment complexity without requiring a stronger general theorem or a paper-sized follow-up.

final_claim: For fixed k>=1 and q=2^k Boolean valuation types, graph-edge co-occurrence formulas on one n-world labelled complete S5 frame have model counts M_G(n)=q^n-Σ_{j=1}^{min(q,n)} i_j(G)j!S(n,j). The first q counts recover I_G, so equality of full quantitative spectra iff equality of independence polynomials at fixed q; exact counting for this syntactic fragment and unary n is #P-complete under polynomial-time Turing reductions. P4 and K3 disjoint K1 already yield logically inequivalent equal-spectra two-atom formulas and the failure probability decays asymptotically at i_alpha(G)(alpha/q)^n for fixed graphs with an edge.
limitations: Only one fixed complete S5 equivalence component with n>=1 labelled worlds and k>=1 Boolean atoms; no count of all frames, all unlabelled models or arbitrary S5 formulas.
The equivalence between spectra and independence polynomials is within the fixed Boolean type universe q=2^k; formula encoding/complexity uses q explicit via the type-disjunction syntax.
Hardness is polynomial-time Turing #P completeness, not many-one or parsimonious.
For n=1 edge formulas are all false; inverse requires all first q counts, not just n=1.
Known graph polynomial collision and other textbook ingredients are not claimed novel.
